newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima climbs on reports of bad loan write-off.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima climbs on reports of bad loan write-off.

text.p: Shares in Tobishima Corp climbed on Thursday morning, encouraged by media reports that Yasuda Trust and Banking Co Ltd had decided to write off bad loans including those extended to the Tobishima group, brokers said.
As of 0139 GMT, the shares were up 13 yen at 189, the third-largest percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Thursday that Yasuda Trust and Banking Co Ltd had already decided to write off problem loans worth a total of 300 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1997, including loans extended to the Tobishima group.
Yasuda Trust was not immediately available for comment.

Fuji Bank Ltd, the main creditor bank for debt-ridden Tobishima, said on Thursday that it believed other creditor financial institutions were positively considering the construction company's restructuring programme.
A Fuji spokesman said, however, that they had not yet reached any conclusions about whether or not they would accept the restructuring programme.
They are expected to inform Tobishima of their conclusion by the end of March, he said.
